sources.outlet: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit
sources.quote: From 2012 to 2019, the Tribe used some of the TCSA money to fund tribal operations that were unrelated to tribal schools.
sources.searcher_note: Lower Brule Sioux Tribe v. Dept. of Interior, No. 25-2375. Year-after-year school-fund diversion found in BIA reviews of the tribe's annual audits (FY2016 $6.1M, FY2017 $3.68M, FY2019 $4.8M deficit). Post-cutoff. Says nothing about going-concern opinions or a 10-year streak.

sources.quote: On June 10, 2020, the BIA issued a bill of collection to the Lower Brule Sioux Tribe for $3,679,223 of school funds that an audit determined had been misdirected.
sources.searcher_note: News story on the 8th Circuit ruling; audit-based misuse of federal school funds. Post-cutoff. Original keloland.com URL returned 403.

sources.outlet: U.S. Department of the Interior Office of Inspector General
sources.quote: The Lower Brule Sioux Tribe did not follow applicable requirements in its agreements with the BIA.
sources.searcher_note: OIG audit: tribe did not account for CARES Act funds appropriately. Same entity, noncompliance with federal award terms, one program and period.

sources.outlet: Office of Justice Programs (abstract of DOJ OIG audit)
sources.quote: did not comply with essential award conditions related to grant expenditures, award special conditions, budget management, and program performance
sources.searcher_note: DOJ OIG audit of Lower Brule's OJP grants (fetch reported publication March 2016); covers 2009-2012 spending, before the lead's 2016-2025 window.

sources.quote: The tribe has accumulated long-term debt of almost $33 million, most of it (about $26 million) for long term bond issuances to finance the government's operations.
sources.searcher_note: Pre-window report on Lower Brule finances, debt and prior audit findings (2008 Eide Bailly audit: $780,000 federal water funds misdirected).

sources.quote: Officials found the tribe had over $900,000 in unallowable, unsupported or unreasonable expenses during this four-year period.
sources.searcher_note: Local coverage of the tribe's financial troubles and the DOJ audit; start of the lead's window, no going-concern or single-audit streak.

notes: No source found that reports going-concern doubt in Lower Brule's single audits, a 10-year streak of going concern plus material noncompliance, the 1-of-67,777 ranking, or the $16.7M to $35.7M / $246.2M federal spending figures. Search snippets pointed to singleaudit.org (SARC) recipient profile 460222351 showing a going-concern paragraph from auditor REDW LLC, but the page returned HTTP 403, so no verified quote; it is a data aggregator, not press. Dakota Scout ran 'South Dakota tribe loses bid to stop government from collecting millions in misspent education funds' on 2026-07-09 (thedakotascout.com/p/south-dakota-tribe-loses-bid-to-stop), body paywalled. South Dakota Searchlight 2024-03-28 on tribal audits under Noem returned 403. GAO-25-106741 (2024-11-07) covers tribal single-audit oversight gaps but does not name Lower Brule. Other same-entity audits found but not recorded: EPA OIG grant audit (97% of costs questioned, older), DOI OIG BIA contract audit ($385,127 questioned).
